Those last things stated, are good to do. and let me show you a problem that is happening with walls at intersections. so this is what i see [Image #1] and here is me painting on it to give u a better look. see how there is this coverage gap on the green edge [Image #2] this is when you are making a corner piece. so when i go to skin this, that wall is going to show weird side piece of the other wall
resolution: Closed the wall-corner coverage gap. Root cause: wallJoinRunLimits' u→world flip mirrored quarters 2|3 while localOffset actually mirrors quarters 1|2 — so yaw-90/270 walls grew their corner-join extension at the EMPTY end of the run (the overhang sticking past the corner) and left the real joint open (the green-edge gap that would skin wrong). Fixed the flip and aligned colliders + camera occluders, which carried the same mirrored mapping (two wrongs canceled for collision; the renderer maps through localOffset and showed it). Also ruled that an end a collinear wall continues past is a continuation, not a corner — no extension there, preventing doubled coplanar slabs between collinear neighbors. Verified with visual-box dumps across yaw 0/90/180/270 corner orientations, T-junctions, and straight runs; placed.test.ts 46/46; rjit game verify GREEN 71/71. Commit 31be83e15.
